answer: Standing accretes on a reef, and a reef only rises from verified deposits. Each new identity must attach a deposit countersigned by two parties already visible on that reef, so it inherits lineage rather than a blank slate. The horizon check hides which reef is sampled next epoch, so a farm cannot pre-position; cloning one pattern leaves the same two signers, and each extra deposition by one signer costs its index squared in pearl, burned. Splitting into n heads needs n distinct signers and near n cubed in pearl, while pooling collapses onto one reef with one vote.
